title: Scaling Shores
description: Load balancers, stateless servers and caches: your first million users.

options: Buying a bigger machine with more CPU and RAM
Adding more machines and spreading the load across them
challenges.explanation: Vertical scaling is a bigger box and eventually hits a ceiling. Horizontal scaling adds more boxes, which is how large systems grow, but it needs something to share the traffic.

challenges.prompt: You run 4 app servers. What does a load balancer add?
options: It spreads requests across healthy servers and stops sending to dead ones
challenges.explanation: A load balancer gives clients one address, distributes requests (round robin, least connections and so on) and health-checks the servers behind it.

challenges.prompt: Why do teams keep app servers stateless, storing sessions in a shared store instead of server memory?
options: Any server can handle any request, so you can add or remove servers freely
challenges.explanation: If a session lives in one server's memory, that user is stuck to that server and loses the session when it dies. Stateless servers are interchangeable.

challenges.prompt: Your app is launching tomorrow. One server will not survive. Build an architecture that handles the traffic.
challenges.explanation: 2,000 req/s needs at least 2 app servers, and extra servers do nothing without a load balancer in front. 3 servers keep utilization near 67%, which keeps latency low.

challenges.prompt: In the cache-aside pattern, what happens on a cache miss?
options: Read from the database, then store the result in the cache
Wait for the cache to refresh
challenges.explanation: The app checks the cache first; on a miss it loads from the database and populates the cache so the next read is a hit.

challenges.prompt: The cache is full. Which eviction policy removes the entry that has gone unused the longest?
challenges.explanation: Least Recently Used assumes recent data will be needed again soon. It is the default in many caches and a classic interview build (hash map + doubly linked list).

challenges.prompt: A user updates their profile, but other users still see the old name. What is the most likely cause?
options: A stale cache entry that was never invalidated or expired
challenges.explanation: Caches trade freshness for speed. Delete or update the key when the data changes, and set a TTL as a safety net.

challenges.prompt: A news site: almost all traffic is people reading articles. The single database is melting. Fix it.
challenges.explanation: 4,500 reads/s would need 3 database shards or replicas. A cache answers ~85% of them from memory for far less money. Then add enough app servers behind a load balancer.
